title: Report On The Voice Of China Max Granich, Editor Of The Voice Of China Leaves Shanghai

page_data.en:
Copy for Officer in charge of Branch
D. 7
" A P
Misc. No. 723/36.    Central
                     November 30,    36.
1

Execution of S.S.D. Search Warrant No. 717
issued by Judge Fang at the request of the
Shanghai Public Safety Bureau respecting No.
281 Shantung Road, The Wu Tsau Su Pao Dzo
Bookstore to search and seize a reactionary
publication entitled "The Voice of China."

At about 9.40 A.M., Monday November 30, 1936, D.S.
341 Pitts with Clerk Zung Zuug Oen, C.D.S. 81 (Special
Branch) and Detective Inspector Tsui Yao Toong (朱校史 )
S.P.S.B. came to Central Station and requested assistance
to search the above described bookstore on the authority
of an S.S.D. Court Search Warrant.

Assistance was rendered by D.S.I. Tilton and C.D.S.
287 attached to Central Station which resulted in the
bookstore being visited at about 9.45 A.M. above date when
the following copies of the publication "The Voice of
China" were seized: 19 copies of Oct. 1, 1936; 41 copies
of Oct. 12, 1936; 18 copies of Nov. 1, 1936; 26 copies of
Nov. 15, 1936 and 53 copies of December 1, 1936. The
total number of copies seized were 157.

The proprietor named Beh Wu Chow (贝五洲 ) was
present and handed over to the undersigned a letter dated
November 22, 1936 from the publisher of the publication
named Max Granich, 749 B'Well Road, Eastern Publishing
Company, Shanghai China, stating that the sale of same
was in order and confirmed by Dr. Hung Chi, S.P.S.B.

An application for disposal of the seized property
will be made before the S.S.D. Court on December 1, 1936.

执行由方法官应上海市公安局之请签发的特别巡捕房搜查令第717号，针对山东路281号“五洲书报店”（Wu Tsau Su Pao Dzo Bookstore），以搜查并扣押名为《中国呼声》的反动刊物。

1936年11月30日，星期一，上午约9时40分，警佐341号皮茨（Pitts）携文员庄祖恩（Zung Zuug Oen，特别部81号）及上海市公安局督察崔耀东（朱校史）来到中央捕房，请求依据特别巡捕房法院搜查令协助搜查上述书店。

中央捕房警督蒂尔顿（Tilton）及特别部287号提供了协助，结果于上述日期上午约9时45分对该书店进行了搜查，查获以下《中国呼声》刊物：1936年10月1日刊19份；1936年10月12日刊41份；1936年11月1日刊18份；1936年11月15日刊26份；以及1936年12月1日刊53份。查获总数为157份。

店主贝五洲（Beh Wu Chow）在场，并向签署人递交了一封出版商马克斯·格拉尼奇（Max Granich）于1936年11月22日发出的信函，地址为中国上海倍开尔路749号东方出版公司，信中声明该刊物的销售合规，并已由上海市公安局洪博士（Dr. Hung Chi）确认。

将于1936年12月1日向特别巡捕房法院申请处置被扣物品。

397/S.11.

June 24, 1937.

"Eastern Publishing Company" and Max Granich.

The "Eastern Publishing Company", registered at the U.S.A.,
Consulate General, was established in March, 1936, by Max Gra-
nich, U.S.A. citizen, at Room 334, 874 Bubbling Well Road.
On 15 th March, 1936, the company published the first issue of
a reactionary and violently anti-Japanese periodical written in
the English language with the addition of a Chinese section and
known as "The Voice of China". This journal appears twice month-
ly and is printed by the Mercury Press, 17 Avenue Edward VII,
a company which is also registered at the U.S.A. Consulate Gene-
ral.

Max Granich, editor and publisher of the above mentioned
periodical, was born on 19th March, 1896, in New York City. He
is a graduate of a high-school in California and is reported to
have worked as a journalist on the staff of "The Call", a commu-
nist newspaper published in New York.

On 31 st January 1936, accompanied by his wife Grace Gra-
nich, age 31, born in Oak Harbour Ohio, U.S.A., Granich arrived
in Shanghai from San Francisco aboard the s.s. "President Taft".
He stated that he was a journalist by profession and that his
sojourn in China would be for an indefinite period. He is in
possession of U.S.A. Passport N°184280 issued on 30th April,
1935, at Washington,D.C.; his wife holds U.S.A. Passport
N°184158 issued on 30th april, 1935, at Washington, D.C. Both
passports were visaed at the Chinese Consulate in New York on
30th December, 1935.

Before her marriage Mrs.Granich was known as Grace Neal, a
frequent contributor of articles to "The United Front", the offi-
cial organ of the Communist Party in America. She is also known
to have been associated with a Miss Harrison and a Miss Wilkinson.

397/S.11.

1937年6月24日。

“东方出版公司”及马克斯·格拉尼奇。

“东方出版公司”在美国总领事馆注册，由美国公民马克斯·格拉尼奇（Max Granich）于1936年3月在倍开尔路874号334室成立。1936年3月15日，该公司出版了第一期反动且激烈反日的英文期刊，附设中文栏目，名为《中国呼声》。该期刊半月刊，由爱德华七世大道17号的水星印刷厂（Mercury Press）印刷，该公司亦在美国总领事馆注册。

上述期刊的编辑兼出版商马克斯·格拉尼奇，1896年3月19日出生于纽约市。他是加州一所高中的毕业生，据报曾在纽约出版的共产党报纸《号召报》（The Call）担任记者。

1936年1月31日，格拉尼奇在其妻子格蕾丝·格拉尼奇（Grace Granich，31岁，出生于美国俄亥俄州奥克港）的陪同下，乘坐“塔夫脱总统号”轮船从旧金山抵达上海。他声称其职业为记者，在华停留期限不定。他持有1935年4月30日在华盛顿特区签发的美国护照第184280号；其妻子持有1935年4月30日在华盛顿特区签发的美国护照第184158号。两本护照均于1935年12月30日在纽约的中国领事馆办理了签证。

格兰尼奇夫人婚前名为格蕾丝·尼尔（Grace Neal），经常向美国共产党的官方机关报《统一战线》（The United Front）投稿文章。据悉她还曾与哈里森小姐（Miss Harrison）和威尔金森小姐（Miss Wilkinson）有往来。

both active communists, the former being at one time the secreta-
ry to Earl Browder.

On arrival in Shanghai Mr.and Mrs.Granich put up at the Bur-
lington Hotel and on 3rd February, 1936 they removed to Room
° II,Cathay Mansions. Shortly after their removal they made a
trip to Peiping where they remained for a week and then returned
to Shanghai. On 3rd March the pair left the Cathay Mansions and
took up residence at Apartment 22, No17# Route Paul Henri, which
address they still occupy.

On 17th March, two days after the first issue had been pu-
blished, Granich, promising that the periodical would be neutral
in character, made application to the French Police to publish
and sell his periodical "The Voice of China" in the French Con-
cession. In reply to his request the French Authorities gave him
verbal permission to print one issue, following which they sta-
ted that they would consider his application for registration.

In spite of Granich's assurances perusal of "The Voice of
China" showed that its policy was anything but neutral. Radical
to an extreme and violently anti-Japanese it urged the people
of China to unite and revolt against Japanese Imperialism, the
tone becoming so reactionary that the Chinese Authorities brought
the matter to the notice of the Municipal Council requesting that
the publication of the magazine be stopped. Information concer-
ning this request was passed to the U.S.A. Consul-General who at
once cancelled the registration of the "Far Eastern Publishing
Company"." Municipal Police together with members of the Police
Bureau conducted several raids in the Settlement and large quan-
tities of "The Voice of China" were seized; publication, however,
much to the annoyance of the Chinese authorities continued.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

两人均为活跃的共产党员，前者曾任厄尔·白劳德（Earl Browder）的秘书。

格拉尼奇夫妇抵达上海后入住伯灵顿饭店（Burlington Hotel），并于1936年2月3日搬至华懋公寓（Cathay Mansions）11号房间。搬家后不久，他们前往北平旅行，停留一周后返回上海。3月3日，二人离开华懋公寓，迁居至亨利·保罗路17号22室公寓，该地址为其现住址。

3月17日，即在第一期出版两天后，格拉尼奇承诺该期刊性质中立，向法租界警方申请在法租界出版和销售其期刊《中国呼声》。作为对其请求的回复，法国当局口头允许其印刷一期，随后表示将考虑其注册申请。

尽管格拉尼奇作出保证，但查阅《中国呼声》显示其政策绝非中立。该刊极端激进且激烈反日，呼吁中国人民团结起来反抗日本帝国主义，其语调如此反动，以致中国当局将此事项提请注意工部局，要求停止该杂志的出版。有关此请求的信息已转达给美国总领事，后者随即取消了“远东出版公司”的注册。工部局警务处会同警察局成员在租界内进行了多次突击搜查，查获大量《中国呼声》；然而，令中国当局极为恼火的是，该刊的出版仍在继续。

page_data.en:
- 3 -

In a further attempt to check Granich's activities the
Chinese Authorities placed a ban on the postal transmission
of "The Voice of China". Several thousand copies were confis-
cated by the local branch of the Post Office and Granich made a
verbal complaint to the U.S.A. Consulate-General. The latter,
however, took no step in the matter and Granich subsequently
made a personal appeal to Mr.Chao Lih Ts (赵力子), Chief of
the Publicity Department of the Central Tangpu, and after pled-
ging loyalty to the Central Government and promising that no-
thing communistic should appear in his journal, was promised that
the ban on transmission would be lifted.

It is reported that Granich has received considerable
assistance and advice from prominent members of the National
Salvation Association in the production of his journal. In
this respect Sung Chun-Shih (沈钧儒), Li Kung Poh (李公朴)
and Miss Sz Liang (史良) are mentioned. Much space is fre-
quently devoted to articles concerning the Association and
contributions on this subject are invited to be sent to
Madame Sun Yat Sen.

Efforts to identify the persons responsible for the au-
thorship of the articles appearing in the journal have been un-
successful; pseudonyms are used, but it is believed that Gra-
nich, assisted by his wife, writes most of them himself. His
office staff consists of himself, his wife, one Yue Chi Chung
(俞之中) alias Yue Woo (俞和) and two Chinese clerks.
Yue is a native of Ningpo, age about 25 years, who resides at
232 Alabaster Road.

That Granich's interests as editor of "The Voice of
China" are political and not financial seems fairly clear. Bear-
ing in mind his advocacy of the principles of the National
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

为进一步遏制格拉尼奇的活动，中国当局禁止邮寄《中国呼声》。邮局当地分局没收了数千份刊物，格拉尼奇向美国总领事馆提出口头抗议。然而，后者在此事上未采取任何行动，随后格拉尼奇亲自向中央党部宣传处处长赵力子（Chao Lih Ts）求助，在宣誓效忠中央政府并承诺其期刊中不会出现任何共产主义内容后，获允解除邮寄禁令。

据报，格拉尼奇在制作其期刊过程中得到了全国救国会知名成员的大量协助和建议。在此方面，提及的人物有沈钧儒（Sung Chun-Shih）、李公朴（Li Kung Poh）和史良小姐（Sz Liang）。该刊经常刊登大量关于该协会的文章，并邀请就此主题投稿寄给孙逸仙夫人。

试图查明期刊文章作者的努力均未成功；文章使用笔名，但据信大部分由格拉尼奇在其妻子协助下亲自撰写。其办公室职员包括他自己、其妻子、一名俞之中（Yue Chi Chung），别名俞和（Yue Woo），以及两名华人职员。俞系宁波人，年龄约25岁，居住于阿尔巴斯特路232号。

格拉尼奇作为《中国呼声》编辑的利益在于政治而非财务，这一点似乎相当明确。鉴于他倡导全国救国会的原则，以及共产党利用该团体推进自身目的的方式，再考虑到他和其妻子在美国与党的关联，几乎可以毫无疑问地认为，格拉尼奇是受共产党派遣前往上海，专门为了出版一本宣传杂志。

page_data.en:
- 4 -

Salvation association and the manner in which the Communist
Party used this group to further its own ends, remembering his
and his wife's association with the Party in the U.S.A., there
seems little doubt that Cranich was sent to Shanghai by the Com-
munist Party with the express purpose of publishing a propaganda
magazine.

The magazine continues to appear fortnightly and is as vir-
ulently anti-Japanese as ever. There has, however, as yet
been no official protest from the Japanese Authorities.
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

该杂志继续每两周出版一期，其反日情绪依然极其激烈。然而，截至目前，日本当局尚未提出正式抗议。
